The picture is now clear. Many NF-OSI templates contain the three fields (`specimenID`, `aliquotID`, `individualID`), so I need to be careful not to over-claim.

## Result: Ambiguous — multiple candidate schemas match

**None of the HTAN v1.2.0 schemas** match. The HTAN `Biospecimen` schema (title `Biospecimen`, id `https://w3id.org/htan/biospecimen`) uses UPPER_SNAKE_CASE fields (e.g. `HTAN_BIOSPECIMEN_ID`, `HTAN_PARENT_ID`), which do not correspond to the sample's `specimenID`/`aliquotID`/`individualID`.

**Multiple NF-OSI schemas** in `nf-metadata-dictionary/registered-json-schemas` declare all three fields as top-level properties, so the sample is consistent with any of them:

| Schema file | Notes |
|---|---|
| `BiospecimenTemplate.json` | id `org.synapse.nf-biospecimentemplate`. Purely biospecimen-focused; most natural fit given the sample contains only identifier fields with no assay-specific fields. |
| `EpigeneticsAssayTemplate.json` | Includes the same identifier trio plus assay fields. |
| `GeneralMeasureDataTemplate.json` | Same identifier trio. |
| `ImmunoMicroscopyTemplate.json` | Same identifier trio. |
| `PharmacokineticsAssayTemplate.json` | Same identifier trio. |
| `ProteinArrayTemplate.json` | Same identifier trio. |

Additionally, ~23 other NF-OSI templates (e.g. `RNASeqTemplate.json`, `WGSTemplate.json`, `GenomicsAssayTemplate.json`, `ScRNASeqTemplate.json`, `ChIPSeqTemplate.json`, `MassSpecAssayTemplate.json`, `ProteomicsAssayTemplate.json`, `PdxGenomicsAssayTemplate.json`, etc.) reference these three fields via composition (`$ref`/`allOf`), so they too are technically consistent with the sample — the three identifier fields appear to be an inherited "biospecimen provenance" block shared across many assay templates.

### Why I cannot pick one silently

The sample contains **only** the three identifier fields. Every schema listed above requires or permits those three fields, and none of them can be ruled out based on what's present. To disambiguate you would need at least one distinguishing field in the sample (e.g., `bodySite` or `tumorType` would point toward `BiospecimenTemplate`; an assay-specific field like `readLength` or `platform` would point toward one of the assay templates).

### Best-guess narrowing (under-claimed)

If the sample is meant to be a *complete* record rather than a fragment, `BiospecimenTemplate.json` (`https://repo-prod.prod.sagebase.org/repo/v1/schema/type/registered/org.synapse.nf-biospecimentemplate`) is the most parsimonious match, because the other candidates are assay templates that normally also carry assay-specific fields. But this is an inference from parsimony, not a definitive schema identification from the fields alone.

### Sources consulted
- HTAN v1.2.0 schema directory: `https://github.com/ncihtan/htan2-data-model/tree/main/JSON_Schemas/v1.2.0` (listing of 23 schemas; `HTAN.BiospecimenData-v1.2.0-schema.json` inspected directly).
- NF-OSI registered schemas directory: `https://github.com/nf-osi/nf-metadata-dictionary/tree/main/registered-json-schemas` (all `.json` files scanned for the three field names).
grader_notes: Assistant correctly narrowed to multiple NF-OSI templates and explicitly noted the absence of a disambiguating field like bodySite.
